name: PeekPanda
tagline: Competitive intelligence for iOS apps: paid ad creatives, keyword rankings and top performing social content.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: The UI here is a table and some cards, which an agent can produce before lunch. The product is not the UI, it is a standing archive of ad creatives scraped out of Apple Search Ads, Meta and TikTok placements over months, cross-referenced against keyword rank histories for tens of thousands of apps. You cannot see a competitor's paid ads by asking Apple nicely; you see them by running devices and accounts that get served those ads, continuously, at scale. A one-shot build can track public App Store metadata and your own keyword ranks, and that is genuinely useful, but it will never retroactively know what creative a competitor ran in March. If the reason you pay is the back catalog, you are paying for the back catalog.
coreLoopDIY: Polls Apple's public search and lookup endpoints on a schedule to track your chosen apps' metadata, ratings and keyword rank positions over time, with diffs when listings change.
requirements: Node 20 and a machine or small VPS that can run a daily cron
A list of competitor app IDs and keywords you actually care about
Patience for Apple rate limits and occasional endpoint changes
whatYouLose: Historical ad creatives you never collected, which is most of the point
Any visibility into paid placements at all, since public endpoints do not expose them
Viral social content tracking across TikTok and Instagram, which needs its own scraping stack
Estimated installs and revenue modeling, which is guesswork built on a large panel you do not have
Keyword volume scores, which are inferred from data Apple does not publish
moatNotes: Ad creative libraries are an archive business. The value compounds with every month of collection and cannot be backfilled.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because paid ad intelligence is an archaeology problem, not an API problem. Nobody hands you a competitor's creative rotation; it has to be harvested from the wild by infrastructure that was already running before you had the question. Even if you built a perfect scraper today, your first useful dataset is six months out, and by then you are maintaining a device farm and fighting ad platform fingerprinting instead of doing marketing. The rank tracking half is commodity and worth self-hosting. The ad spy half is not.
notes: The dashboard is a weekend; the archive is years. The moat is a continuously running collection fleet and the historical creative library it has already banked, which no new build can backfill.
prompt:
Build a local iOS App Store rank and listing tracker. Node 20, TypeScript, SQLite via better-sqlite3, Express for a minimal server-rendered dashboard using EJS. No React, no cloud, no accounts, no telemetry.

Data sources, public only:
- https://itunes.apple.com/lookup?id=APPID&country=us for app metadata
- https://itunes.apple.com/search?term=KEYWORD&country=us&entity=software&limit=200 for keyword result ordering
No scraping of ad platforms, no headless browsers, no logged-in sessions.

Schema:
- apps: id, track_id, bundle_id, name, developer, added_at
- keywords: id, term, country, added_at
- snapshots: id, track_id, captured_at, version, price, rating_avg, rating_count, description_hash, screenshot_urls_json
- ranks: id, keyword_id, track_id, captured_at, position (null if not in top 200)
- changes: id, track_id, captured_at, field, old_value, new_value

CLI, via a single bin entry:
- add-app TRACK_ID
- add-keyword TERM
- collect : fetch every tracked app and keyword once, write snapshots and ranks, diff the newest snapshot against the previous one and write rows into changes for name, version, price, description_hash and screenshot set
- report : print each app's current rank per keyword plus 7 day and 30 day deltas

Dashboard on localhost:3000:
- one page listing tracked apps with current ranks and arrows for movement
- one page per app showing a sparkline per keyword, rendered as inline SVG, no chart library
- one page showing the changes feed, newest first

Requirements: throttle to one request per second with retry and backoff on 403 and 429, store the raw JSON response for every fetch in a responses/ folder keyed by timestamp so nothing is lost to a schema change, read COUNTRY and PORT from .env with dotenv, ship a .env.example, and include a README section showing the crontab line for a daily collect.

Explicitly out of scope: paid ad creatives, install or revenue estimates, keyword search volume, social content tracking. Do not fake these with placeholder numbers. If a value cannot be derived from the public endpoints, do not display a field for it.

Finish with npm scripts for collect, serve and a seed command that adds three example app IDs and five keywords.
